home: a three-bedroom suburban house with a garage and a laundry room
layout_thinking: A practical 1,850-square-foot suburban house with a front entry, open living and dining areas, a compact kitchen, three distinct bedrooms, one hall bathroom, a laundry room, and an attached two-car garage. Storage is distributed realistically, with the older bedroom having a smaller closet and the garage carrying household overflow.

places.furniture: four-burner gas stovetop
places.name: front-left burner
descriptions: The medium burner nearest the kitchen island.
Usually marked by a faint ring of baked-on tomato sauce.
Its black grate lifts off for cleaning.

places.furniture: four-burner gas stovetop
places.name: front-right burner
descriptions: The larger burner in front of the range controls.
The couple uses it for the stockpot and cast-iron skillet.
Its grate has a small silver chip along one corner.

places.furniture: four-burner gas stovetop
places.name: back-left burner
descriptions: A small burner toward the backsplash.
Often used for the kettle or a saucepan.
The enamel around it is cleaner than the front burners.

places.furniture: four-burner gas stovetop
places.name: back-right burner
descriptions: The medium rear burner beside the stove's back-right corner.
A heat-darkened ring surrounds the burner cap.
It is partly shaded by the raised range hood.

places.furniture: range oven
places.name: oven interior
descriptions: The lower oven cavity beneath the stovetop.
A dark enamel floor holds a removable rack and a shallow roasting pan when in use.
The back panel has a small patch of baked-on grease.

places.furniture: kitchen sink
places.name: sink basin
descriptions: The single deep stainless-steel basin between the two counter sections.
A removable black drain strainer sits at the bottom.
The faucet's short hose reaches most of the basin but not the far corner.

places.furniture: dish rack and drying mat
places.name: dish-drying mat
descriptions: A charcoal-gray ribbed mat beside the sink.
It usually holds two mugs and whatever cannot go in the dishwasher.
The right edge curls upward where it has dried repeatedly.

places.furniture: dishwasher
places.name: dishwasher interior
descriptions: The stainless-lined dishwasher cavity beneath the counter to the right of the sink.
The lower rack has one bent tine that is used for plates at an angle.
A blue detergent tab is sometimes left in the dispenser until evening.

places.furniture: countertop microwave
places.name: microwave interior
descriptions: The white enamel cavity on the shelf above the counter.
A round glass turntable sits inside.
There is a faint orange stain on the back wall from reheated curry.

residents.name: Mara Ellis
residents.personality: Methodical, warm, and quietly observant. Mara likes a plan but is not especially tidy while she is in the middle of something; she leaves little islands of paperwork, tea, and opened books around the house. She notices household problems early and keeps trying to solve them with labels, baskets, and reminders.

weekly_routine.activity: Coffee, toast, and checking the weather and transit alerts before work
Commute to the municipal office
Transportation planning work, meetings, and reviewing street-project maps
Answering a few messages and sorting mail
Grocery shopping and picking up prescriptions
Working from home on a neighborhood traffic-calming proposal
Dinner and conversation with Daniel
Gentle stretching and a television episode
Reading a library book with tea
Laundry, changing the bed linens, and folding clothes
Farmers market and errands
Coffee, crossword, and weekly calendar planning
Preparing vegetables and a casserole for the coming week

object_habits: My reading glasses live on the left nightstand, although I regularly carry them downstairs and forget them on the living-room side table.
I put incoming mail in a neat stack on the left end of the dining table until I have time to sort it.
My work laptop stays in its padded backpack on the bedroom-two desk when I work from home and goes to the office with me on other weekdays.
I keep a blue ceramic mug at the kitchen island center and become mildly annoyed when Daniel uses it for screws or paintbrush water.
I leave grocery lists under the small magnet on the refrigerator door, then transfer the useful items to my phone before shopping.
My house keys usually land in the maple console's left drawer, but on rushed mornings I leave them on the entry console top.

response_habits.trigger: When work becomes politically tense or a project deadline moves suddenly
response_habits.behavior: I take a brisk twenty-minute walk around the corner lot and nearby streets before trying to talk about it.

response_habits.trigger: When Daniel feels sick or has had a difficult day
response_habits.behavior: I make ginger tea and put it on the right side of the living-room coffee table without asking many questions.

response_habits.trigger: When I am too tired to cook after a long meeting day
response_habits.behavior: I order Thai food and eat it at the dining table while apologizing that I did not plan ahead.

response_habits.trigger: When the house feels visually crowded
response_habits.behavior: I do a fast reset of the entry, sofa, and kitchen counters before I can relax.

scheduled_stressors: Monday morning staff meeting where project delays are discussed
Wednesday evening grocery trip after a full workday
Thursday deadline for sending revised traffic plans to neighborhood groups
Monthly Sunday evening budget review with Daniel

residents.name: Daniel Ellis
residents.personality: Practical, patient with machines, and sociable in short bursts. Daniel is affectionate but easily distracted by a loose hinge, odd noise, or item that could be repaired rather than replaced. He dislikes schedules that change without warning and leaves evidence of ongoing projects wherever he happens to stop.

weekly_routine.activity: Shower, pack tools, and eat a quick breakfast
Driving between appliance repair calls
Changing out of work clothes and checking the next day's service calls
Cleaning and restocking the service van
Cooking dinner, usually something from the grill pan or a one-pot meal
Stopping for takeout or reheating Mara's prepared food
Watching television, repairing small household items, or reading sports news
Garage projects, tool maintenance, and seasonal house repairs
Hardware store, car wash, and other errands
Making a late breakfast and cleaning the kitchen
Calling his mother and sorting service receipts

object_habits: My truck keys go on the entry coat rack's middle-right hook, while my work keys stay clipped to my belt until I am home.
I leave a tape measure or screwdriver on the living-room media console whenever I notice something that needs measuring.
My work boots sit on the lower shoe-rack shelf, but muddy boots get left on the floor beside it until I remember to clean them.
I keep spare appliance parts in labeled coffee cans on the left garage shelving, even though the labels are mostly handwritten abbreviations only I understand.
My wallet goes in the right nightstand drawer every night; if it is not there, it is probably in yesterday's work pants in the laundry hamper.
I carry a pocket notebook and set it on the kitchen counter right of the stove while cooking, where it sometimes acquires grease spots.
I use the bottom shelf of the leaning living-room bookshelf for manuals and catalogs, which makes the already sagging shelf bow a little more.

response_habits.trigger: When a customer cancels late or a repair call goes badly
response_habits.behavior: I spend twenty or thirty minutes doing a small, definite repair in the garage rather than discussing the problem immediately.

response_habits.trigger: When I get home after an overloaded route
response_habits.behavior: I skip cooking, suggest sandwiches or takeout, and sit on the sofa before changing out of my work shirt.

response_habits.trigger: When I have missed lunch or been stuck in traffic
response_habits.behavior: I become terse and start rummaging for food in the pantry until Mara points it out.

response_habits.trigger: When Mara is upset but does not want advice
response_habits.behavior: I make coffee, sit nearby, and fix or sharpen something quietly instead of asking repeated questions.

scheduled_stressors: Monday and Thursday routes with tightly packed repair appointments
Friday afternoon service-van inventory and paperwork
Customers who cancel after he has already driven across town
Saturday morning garage projects that run longer than planned

situations.what_it_is_like: One of them comes down with a short-lived cold or stomach bug and feels abruptly reduced to the basics: sleep, water, quiet, and getting through the day. The sick person is frustrated by being unable to keep up with ordinary responsibilities and becomes more dependent than either of them prefers. The well person takes over more of the practical work, checks in often, and tries not to make care feel like supervision.
situations.what_others_notice: The sick resident is quieter, slower, and less interested in conversation, with a shorter temper when discomfort lingers. The well resident becomes unusually attentive and restrained, speaking softly and watching for signs that the illness is worsening, though Daniel may fuss and Mara may over-organize the recovery.

situations.what_it_is_like: A major transportation proposal or public meeting gives Mara several days of concentrated pressure. She is mentally elsewhere even when she is present, rehearsing explanations and worrying about overlooked details. She sleeps lightly, eats later than usual, and feels relief only in brief moments when a complicated point finally makes sense.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel notices that Mara answers accurately but only halfway listens, then circles back to clarify what he said. She becomes more formal in her speech, more easily bothered by interruptions, and visibly relaxes when she can explain a problem aloud without being hurried.

situations.what_it_is_like: A repair job runs long because the real fault is hidden or a customer has one more question. Daniel is tired but keyed up, replaying the machine's symptoms and feeling responsible for leaving a job unresolved. He wants to tell Mara the whole story, even when he has little energy left for anything else.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel arrives later and more slowly than usual, with a distracted intensity that makes him seem physically present but mentally still at work. He talks in bursts about the problem, then goes quiet while mentally diagnosing it again.

situations.what_it_is_like: A colleague or neighbor comes for dinner, and both residents become more socially alert than they expected. Mara quietly monitors whether everyone is comfortable, while Daniel warms up through practical stories and short jokes. They are pleased afterward but need a calm evening to recover from being hosts.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara seems gracious and prepared, though she occasionally disappears into thought while checking that the evening is going smoothly. Daniel is initially reserved, then becomes animated once the guest asks about his work; afterward he is friendly but ready for solitude.

situations.what_it_is_like: A call from Mara's parent turns into an unplanned account of a minor health worry, family disagreement, or administrative problem. Mara listens patiently while feeling the old pull to be competent and reassuring. Even after the call ends, she keeps wondering whether she missed something important.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara's voice becomes especially gentle and careful, and she asks more questions than usual. Afterward she may seem composed but preoccupied, bringing the conversation up again in fragments as she sorts out what she feels responsible for.

situations.what_it_is_like: A relative stays for a short visit, bringing affection, opinions, and a mild disruption to the couple's established rhythm. Mara tries to anticipate needs and prevent awkwardness. Daniel is welcoming in doses, then seeks brief stretches without conversation so he can regain patience.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara becomes more accommodating and slightly tense, smoothing over differences before anyone else notices them. Daniel is sociable at first and then noticeably more distracted, answering from another room or drifting toward whatever practical problem has caught his attention.

situations.what_it_is_like: Bad weather makes both commutes slower and more tiring. Mara arrives already thinking through delays and contingency plans, while Daniel is irritated by how much time was lost to conditions nobody could control. They are glad to be together but have less patience than usual.
situations.what_others_notice: They speak more tersely and move with heavy, end-of-day caution. Mara wants to account for every delay; Daniel wants the subject dropped. Their irritation passes quickly once they have eaten and warmed up.

situations.what_it_is_like: Mara leads a contentious evening meeting about a street redesign or transit change. She feels responsible for making technical information fair and understandable, while also bracing for anger from people who believe the plan threatens their routines. She is proud if she remains patient, even when the discussion becomes personal.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara returns mentally exhausted but unusually alert, speaking precisely and recounting exact phrases people used. She may seem calm on the surface while continuing to evaluate what she should have said differently.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel's work truck develops a serious fault, leaving him stranded between jobs and worried about lost income and the inconvenience to customers. He is embarrassed to need help with a problem he would normally solve for someone else. Once the immediate crisis passes, curiosity and professional pride begin replacing the anxiety.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel is unusually quiet at first and tries to minimize the trouble. He becomes restless while waiting, then animatedly explains possible causes, alternating between self-criticism and confidence that he can understand what happened.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel attends a technical training course covering unfamiliar equipment and newer diagnostic methods. He dislikes being treated like a beginner but enjoys discovering a clever approach. The long days leave him tired, and he worries that the training will expose gaps in his knowledge.
situations.what_others_notice: He returns more talkative and mentally energized than physically rested. He tests new explanations out loud, accepts Mara's questions more readily than usual, and seems quietly pleased when he can teach her something.

situations.what_it_is_like: Mara begins working from home several weekdays after a change in her department's schedule. She appreciates the saved commute and the chance to concentrate, but the boundary between working time and personal time becomes indistinct. She feels guilty when she is technically home but unavailable, and restless when she ends the day without a clear transition.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara is present more often but not necessarily more available. Daniel notices her becoming absorbed and quiet during the day, then making a deliberate effort to reconnect in the evening as if switching roles requires conscious preparation.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel is assigned an earlier service route, changing the shape of mornings and leaving him ready for bed sooner at night. He likes finishing before traffic worsens but misses the slower start and feels vaguely out of step with Mara. His energy is best early and fades sharply later.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel moves briskly in the morning and has little patience for last-minute changes. In the evening he is affectionate but visibly worn down, sometimes stopping mid-sentence because his attention and energy have run out.

situations.what_it_is_like: Mara takes up balcony gardening after realizing she wants an activity with no deadline or public consequence. She enjoys observing gradual change and learning by trial and error, though she makes careful plans even for a small experiment. The hobby gives her a quiet mental refuge from work.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara becomes more patient when discussing small failures and more willing to leave a question unresolved. She talks about weather, growth, and timing with a soft enthusiasm Daniel does not often hear in her work stories.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel starts restoring an old household appliance as a personal project rather than a job. He enjoys the mystery and the chance to work without a customer waiting, but the project keeps expanding as he discovers new faults. He feels protective of it and defensive when Mara suggests setting a stopping point.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel becomes absorbed, patient, and unusually unwilling to call anything finished. He talks to the appliance as though it has a personality, and his mood improves whenever a stubborn problem yields.

situations.what_it_is_like: An evening outage interrupts both residents' plans and removes the usual background of work and entertainment. Mara initially wants to establish a sensible sequence for the next few hours; Daniel immediately starts investigating the cause. Once they accept that they cannot hurry the restoration, the interruption becomes unexpectedly companionable.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara shifts from controlled concern to amused resignation. Daniel is restless and eager to help, but gradually settles into conversation, seeming pleased that a practical emergency has given him a clear shared purpose.

situations.what_it_is_like: A demanding week causes them both to overlook a relationship anniversary until late in the day. Mara feels disappointed and interprets the omission as evidence that they have become too operational. Daniel feels guilty and tries to repair the mood quickly, though his first attempts are clumsy.
situations.what_others_notice: They are unusually careful with one another, each waiting for the other to reveal how hurt they are. The tension is quiet rather than explosive, and both become warmer once they admit that exhaustion, not indifference, was responsible.

situations.what_it_is_like: A dispute over noise, parking, or a shared boundary pulls them into an uncomfortable exchange with neighbors. Mara wants facts and a fair process; Daniel wants the matter settled without turning it into a permanent relationship. Both feel protective of their home and annoyed that they have to defend ordinary peace.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara becomes measured and formal, while Daniel becomes blunt and physically restless. They may disagree about how much to engage, but afterward they compare impressions carefully and recognize that each handled a different part of the conflict.

situations.what_it_is_like: A family member shares genuinely good news, such as a new job, recovery, engagement, or move. The couple enjoys the happiness but also gets pulled into questions about timing, money, and whether they should help. Mara thinks ahead; Daniel responds more spontaneously and warmly.
situations.what_others_notice: Both are lighter and more generous than usual. Mara asks practical follow-up questions, while Daniel tells the story again with increasing delight and makes affectionate predictions about what will happen next.

situations.what_it_is_like: After a demanding stretch, they intentionally keep a weekend nearly empty. Mara enjoys having no decisions to make but initially feels she ought to be productive. Daniel relaxes more quickly, though he may become bored and invent a minor task before remembering that rest was the point.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara seems softer and less vigilant by the second day. Daniel becomes playful and more physically affectionate, then briefly restless whenever the quiet lasts longer than he expected.

small_disturbances.text: A message from her supervisor asks for one small revision that turns into an hour of checking figures.
A customer calls to say the repaired appliance has started making a different noise.
The milk is gone when someone starts making breakfast.
A package arrives for the neighbor, and nobody answers when they knock.
She cannot remember whether she already moved an appointment into her phone calendar.
He finds a loose screw in the kitchen and spends several minutes trying to identify where it came from.
The smoke alarm chirps once and then stops.
A transit alert warns of delays on her usual route.
His work dispatcher changes the order of two calls just as he is leaving.
A relative calls with a question that begins casually and becomes complicated.
She realizes she has left her reading glasses upstairs after settling in downstairs.
He notices a muddy mark near the entry and tries to determine whether it came from him or a visitor.
The internet connection drops during an important video call.
A grocery item on the handwritten list is unavailable, requiring an improvised substitute.
He cannot find his wallet and reconstructs the previous day's route aloud.
A neighbor asks whether the unusual sound outside came from their home.
An email arrives with a deadline earlier than she had recorded.
A hinge begins squeaking loudly enough to distract him from dinner.
